column5: FIBA carries ONE club per player and chose her WNBA side, Connecticut Sun — which is right for the Club column and is what we would have overridden Wikipedia to say. But she plays for both, and her Turkish club is real and interesting on a Türkiye roster page. FIBA's single Club field cannot hold two, which is exactly why the Note column exists. Carried forward from overrides-2026-09-03.tsv.

FIBA registers her under her maiden name. She married Ben DiLeo in 2023 and has played under DiLeo since; the WNBA, ESPN and our own player page at /players/megan-dileo/ all use it. Jason 2026-09-03: FIBA not respecting her married name is FIBA's bureaucracy, not a fact about her name. A person's own name beats a registration form. Delete this row to publish FIBA's form instead — and note `player_href`'s ALIASES still maps the box-score spelling "Megan Gustafson" to /megan-dileo/, so her link works either way.

The only genuinely new player in the FIBA capture — she was not on Mali's 22-name preselection, so there was no existing spelling to keep. FIBA's name fields are ASCII-stripped, so its "Naignouma" is not evidence of no accent. Wikipedia's squads page, re-checked 2026-09-03 after it was updated to Mali's final 12, spells her Naîgnouma with a circumflex and gives the same date of birth (1989-05-31), so this is the same player and the accent is real.

FIBA's WWC entry drops half her surname. Every other source keeps it — ESPN, Basketball-Reference, Eurobasket, and FIBA's OWN 2026 qualifying-tournament page (player 271903, slug "pallas-kunaiyi-akpanah"); her full name is Pallas Daemi Kunaiyi-Akpanah. So this is a truncated field, not a name she changed, and FIBA contradicts itself on it. Same call as the Megan DiLeo row above: where a governing body's registration SUBTRACTS a name, it is evidence of a form field, not of the person's wishes.
